points: Q2 2026 is already reported and showed adjusted EPS of $1.49 versus a $0.99 consensus, plus margin improvement; the Q3 print will reveal whether that earnings momentum and margin expansion carried into the new quarter.
Q2 revenue missed, so the Q3 print will show whether top-line growth is reaccelerating toward the +15.04% 90-day estimate direction or if demand remains soft.

Analysts have raised estimates 2-to-0 over the last 30 days; Q3 results and any guidance update will test whether the FY1/FY2 EPS estimates of $4.71/$5.43 and 13.9%/15.4% growth still have room to move higher.
Reports suggest the Brink’s merger is moving toward a 2027 close; management commentary on integration timing, synergies, and deal progress will shape the FY2 setup.
NATL trades at a P/E of about 9.78x, roughly 0.7x the theme median, with a PEG near 0.70x; the print needs to confirm the earnings growth path is intact to support a valuation re-rating.

Peer prints from GPN, JKHY, PAYO, EVTC and CPAY around the same week will provide sector read-throughs on transaction and payment processing demand; NATL’s Q3 results will show whether it is participating in or diverging from that tone.
watch: Q3 revenue growth versus the +15.04% 90-day estimate direction — supports the long if it tracks or exceeds that upward trend.
FY1/FY2 EPS estimate revision direction around $4.71/$5.43 and 13.9%/15.4% growth — supports the long if analysts keep raising estimates.
Adjusted margin trajectory after Q2’s margin improvement — supports the long if margins hold or expand rather than revert.
P/E discount to theme (~0.7x median) and PEG (~0.70x) versus earnings growth — supports the long if the valuation gap persists while growth stays on track.
